record.original_question: Let a bounded operator T on a complex Hilbert space be complex symmetric if T = C T* C for some conjugation C. Normal operators can be decomposed using multiplication operators M_z on spaces L^2(X, mu). Is there an analogous model theory for complex symmetric operators that plays a comparable structural role for this class, possibly involving truncated Toeplitz operators as candidate model objects?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a separable complex Hilbert space. A conjugation on $\mathcal{H}$ is an antilinear map $C:\mathcal{H}\to\mathcal{H}$ satisfying $C^2 = I$ and $\langle Cx, Cy\rangle = \langle y, x\rangle$ for all $x,y\in\mathcal{H}$. A bounded linear operator $T\in B(\mathcal{H})$ is called complex symmetric if there exists a conjugation $C$ such that $T = CT^*C$.

By the spectral theorem, every bounded normal operator on $\mathcal{H}$ is unitarily equivalent to a direct sum/integral of multiplication operators $M_z f(z) = z f(z)$ on Lebesgue spaces $L^2(X,\mu)$ for compact subsets $X\subset\mathbb{C}$; this provides a complete canonical model for normal operators.

For an inner function $u$ on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $K_u = H^2 \ominus uH^2$ denote the model space inside the Hardy space $H^2$. For $\varphi\in L^2(\partial\mathbb{D})$, the truncated Toeplitz operator $A_\varphi^u$ on $K_u$ is the closure (when bounded) of $f\mapsto P_u(\varphi f)$, where $P_u$ is the orthogonal projection from $L^2(\partial\mathbb{D})$ onto $K_u$. Each $A_\varphi^u$ is complex symmetric with respect to a natural conjugation on $K_u$.

Problem: Develop a structural model theory for bounded complex symmetric operators that plays a role comparable to the multiplication-operator model for normal operators. In particular, determine whether every bounded complex symmetric operator on a separable complex Hilbert space is unitarily equivalent to a direct sum (or direct integral) of truncated Toeplitz operators $A_\varphi^u$ on model spaces $K_u$, and if not, identify the appropriate class of elementary complex symmetric building blocks into which an arbitrary bounded complex symmetric operator can be canonically decomposed.
artifact.status_search_result: The literature treats truncated Toeplitz operators as natural candidate model operators for complex symmetric operators, with partial results on matrix representations and Clark-basis unitary equivalences. A full model theory comparable to the spectral theorem for normal operators has not been established; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Symmetric matrix representations of truncated Toeplitz operators on finite dimensional spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Conditions for a symmetric matrix to be a truncated Toeplitz operator with respect to a conjugation-invariant basis; refined conjecture toward model theory.
status_evidence.claim: A definitive model theory for complex symmetric operators via truncated Toeplitz operators has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Complex symmetric operators (lecture notes by S. R. Garcia)
status_evidence.snippet: Truncated Toeplitz operators serve as candidate model operators for various complex symmetric operators; full model theory still to be developed.
status_evidence.claim: A comparable model theory for complex symmetric operators is not yet known.
